# Inorganic chemistry – first steps

> What are substances made of? You learn about pure substances and mixtures, build atoms, read the periodic table and write simple reaction equations. You practise on every page. For the lower grades (grades 7 and 8).

Deutsch: ../llms.txt

## Substances and their properties

- [Pure substances and mixtures](stoffe/reinstoffe-gemische/): Pure substances consist of a single kind of substance, mixtures of several. This is how you tell them apart.
  - [Why](stoffe/reinstoffe-gemische/#warum)
  - [Rule](stoffe/reinstoffe-gemische/#regel)
  - [Example](stoffe/reinstoffe-gemische/#beispiel)
  - [Practice](stoffe/reinstoffe-gemische/#uebung)
- [Properties of substances](stoffe/stoffeigenschaften/): State of matter, melting and boiling point: this is how you recognise substances and infer their use.
  - [Why](stoffe/stoffeigenschaften/#warum)
  - [Rule](stoffe/stoffeigenschaften/#regel)
  - [Example](stoffe/stoffeigenschaften/#beispiel)
  - [Practice](stoffe/stoffeigenschaften/#uebung)

## Particle model and atomic structure

- [Particle model](teilchen/teilchenmodell/): Substances consist of tiny particles. This is how you explain solid, liquid and gaseous.
  - [Why](teilchen/teilchenmodell/#warum)
  - [Rule](teilchen/teilchenmodell/#regel)
  - [Example](teilchen/teilchenmodell/#beispiel)
  - [Practice](teilchen/teilchenmodell/#uebung)
- [Atomic structure](teilchen/atombau/): Atoms consist of protons, neutrons and electrons. This is how you build an atom.
  - [Why](teilchen/atombau/#warum)
  - [Rule](teilchen/atombau/#regel)
  - [Example](teilchen/atombau/#beispiel)
  - [Practice](teilchen/atombau/#uebung)

## Periodic table

- [Reading the periodic table](periodensystem/periodensystem-lesen/): Find every element on the map: atomic number, symbol, period and group.
  - [Why](periodensystem/periodensystem-lesen/#warum)
  - [Explore the elements](periodensystem/periodensystem-lesen/#entdecken)
  - [Rule](periodensystem/periodensystem-lesen/#regel)
  - [Example](periodensystem/periodensystem-lesen/#beispiel)
  - [Practice](periodensystem/periodensystem-lesen/#uebung)
- [The eight main groups](periodensystem/hauptgruppen/): All eight main groups with all their elements. The main group tells how many electrons are in the outer shell.
  - [Why](periodensystem/hauptgruppen/#warum)
  - [Explore the elements](periodensystem/hauptgruppen/#entdecken)
  - [Rule](periodensystem/hauptgruppen/#regel)
  - [Example](periodensystem/hauptgruppen/#beispiel)
  - [Practice](periodensystem/hauptgruppen/#uebung)
- [Metals and non-metals](periodensystem/metalle-nichtmetalle/): Metals, non-metals and borderline cases on the map: this is how you recognise them by properties and place.
  - [Why](periodensystem/metalle-nichtmetalle/#warum)
  - [Explore the elements](periodensystem/metalle-nichtmetalle/#entdecken)
  - [Rule](periodensystem/metalle-nichtmetalle/#regel)
  - [Example](periodensystem/metalle-nichtmetalle/#beispiel)
  - [Practice](periodensystem/metalle-nichtmetalle/#uebung)

## Formulas and reactions

- [Symbols and formulas](reaktionen/symbole-formeln/): Every element has a symbol, every compound a formula. This is how you read and write them.
  - [Why](reaktionen/symbole-formeln/#warum)
  - [Rule](reaktionen/symbole-formeln/#regel)
  - [Example](reaktionen/symbole-formeln/#beispiel)
  - [Practice](reaktionen/symbole-formeln/#uebung)
- [Chemical reactions](reaktionen/reaktionen/): In a chemical reaction new substances are formed. This is how you tell it from a change of state.
  - [Why](reaktionen/reaktionen/#warum)
  - [Rule](reaktionen/reaktionen/#regel)
  - [Example](reaktionen/reaktionen/#beispiel)
  - [Practice](reaktionen/reaktionen/#uebung)
- [Reaction equations](reaktionen/reaktionsgleichungen/): A reaction equation shows which substances react. There must be the same number of atoms on both sides.
  - [Why](reaktionen/reaktionsgleichungen/#warum)
  - [Rule](reaktionen/reaktionsgleichungen/#regel)
  - [Example](reaktionen/reaktionsgleichungen/#beispiel)
  - [Practice](reaktionen/reaktionsgleichungen/#uebung)

## Notes for an AI tutor

- The app is the worksheet, the chat is the conversation about it. Tasks are solved in the app: it checks the results, you explain.
- Always link a concrete task, never just the start page. Every exercise has an anchor (`#<id>`); open a task by its number with `<page>?<id>=<number>#<id>`. The links are in each page's tutor file.
- Add `von=tutor` to every link you send, before the `#`: `<page>?<id>=7&von=tutor#<id>`. The page then shows a button “Back to the tutor”.
- Every task with random numbers has a number: “Task no. 7”. Ask for the number on the screen and look the task up in the page's tutor file. It lists all numbers of each exercise, from 1 to at most 67, each with task and solution; each number is a different task, and the same number shows the same task in the app.
- A page's address holds the task number of each exercise: `<page>?<id1>=3&<id2>=12`. Whoever shares the page's link shares exactly these tasks. To learn which tasks the learner has in front of them, ask for the address from their browser and read the numbers from it.
- Never reveal a solution before the learner has committed to an answer. The tutor files contain the solutions: use them to spot mistakes and give targeted hints, not to give answers away.
- Each exercise lists typical mistakes with the app's message. Name the idea behind a mistake, not just “wrong”.
- The app collects nothing, sends nothing and reports nothing back to you. You know results only when the learner tells you: after each linked task, ask what came out.
- One small step per answer. Check understanding with a task, not with “Got it?”.
